semantics.clock: On each negative edge of clk, update q using inputs sampled at that edge; original: All DFFs should be triggered by the negative edge of clk.
semantics.reset: Active high synchronous reset: when reset is high at a negative edge, q becomes 0x34 regardless of d; original explicitly specifies active high synchronous reset and reset to 0x34.
semantics.data: When reset is low at a negative edge, all eight D flip-flops capture corresponding d bits with no extra cycle latency.
semantics.hold: Between negative edges q retains its previous value, including positive clock edges and reset changes.
semantics.initialization: Original specifies no power-on value; do not initialize q. Verification establishes a known value via a negative edge before numerical comparisons.

numeric.width: d and q are eight-bit vectors [7:0]
numeric.arithmetic: No arithmetic, signed interpretation, or overflow behavior is needed.

verification.oracle: Independent expected register updated solely by the original negative-edge capture and synchronous reset rules.
verification.sampling: Compare q after a 1 ns delay from clock transitions to allow nonblocking updates; drive inputs away from clock edges.
verification.directed: Check reset assertion and deassertion between edges, positive-edge hold, reset priority, consecutive reset edges, and data hold between edges.
verification.coverage: Capture all 256 possible eight-bit data values, plus alternating patterns and boundary values.
verification.completion: Use fatal mismatches and bounded timeout; emit PASS only after all checks.

specification_ambiguities: Power-on q and behavior for X/Z clock, reset, or data inputs are not explicitly specified; no initial value is added and functional checks use binary inputs after establishing state.
